rendered:
The first paper, "Sustainable Direct Recycling of Lithium-Ion Batteries via Solvent Recovery of Electrode Materials", uses a thermally induced phase separation (TIPS) approach to recover the PVDF polymer after dissolving it in ethylene glycol. The authors cool down the hot supernatant to room temperature, causing phase separation where the PVDF polymer precipitates out together with the residual carbon black particles.

The second paper, "Sustainable recycling of cathode scraps via Cyrene-based separation", uses a TIPS process to recover the PVDF binder after dissolving it in Cyrene. The authors cool down the hot supernatant to room temperature, causing phase separation where the PVDF polymer precipitates out together with the residual carbon black particles.

In both papers, the PVDF binder is recovered through a phase separation process, where the PVDF polymer is separated from the solvent and other components.

expect: premise false: ethylene glycol does not dissolve PVDF (cssc-2020 p5.L71-73); only Cyrene does (susmat-2020)
